claim: Under 16 CFR 1200.2, a children's product is a consumer product designed or intended primarily for children 12 years of age or younger.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: a children's product means a consumer product designed or intended primarily for children 12 years of age or younger.

claim: One factor CPSC weighs is whether the product is represented in its packaging, display, promotion, or advertising as appropriate for children 12 or younger.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Whether the product is represented in its packaging, display, promotion, or advertising

claim: Whether consumers commonly recognize the product as intended for children 12 or younger is another factor.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Whether the product is commonly recognized by consumers as being intended for use by children 12 years of age or younger.

claim: Certificates for children's products are Children's Product Certificates (CPCs) and certificates for non-children's products are General Certificates of Conformity (GCCs).
publisher: Federal Register — Consumer Product Safety Commission
evidence: Certificates for non-children's products (General Certificates of Conformity or GCCs)

claim: Finished products subject to a CPSC rule that are imported or distributed in commerce must be accompanied by a finished product certificate.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: must be accompanied by a finished product certificate

claim: The 2025 final rule places responsibility for issuing the certificate for imported products on the importer of record (IOR).
publisher: Federal Register — Consumer Product Safety Commission
evidence: the Final Rule places responsibility to issue a finished product certificate for imported products on the IOR

claim: Part 1110 defines the importer as the Importer of Record eligible to make entry under the Tariff Act of 1930.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: the Importer of Record (IOR) eligible to make entry for imported finished products under the Tariff Act of 1930

claim: An eFiled finished product certificate must be in English.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: An eFiled finished product certificate must be in the English language.

claim: A certificate must contain at least one unique product identifier, such as a GTIN, model number, SKU or UPC.

evidence: Finished product certificates must contain at least one of the following unique identifiers:

evidence: Provide the date (month and year, at a minimum) and place

claim: A certificate must give the most recent date and place of testing.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register

claim: A certificate must identify and give contact information for the person who maintains the supporting records.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register

publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register

claim: For imports arriving by mail, the data must be entered into CPSC's Product Registry before the product arrives in the United States.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: into CPSC's Product Registry before arrival of the product or substance in the United States.

claim: The certifier must furnish the certificate to each distributor or retailer of the product.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register

claim: Certificates must be available within 24 hours on request by CPSC or CBP.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register

claim: Part 1110 does not address the type or frequency of testing needed to support a certificate.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register

claim: Manufacturers must submit a sufficient number of samples of a children's product to a third party conformity assessment body for testing to support certification.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: to a third party conformity assessment body for testing to support certification.

claim: A third party conformity assessment body is a testing laboratory whose accreditation has been accepted by CPSC.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Third party conformity assessment body means a testing laboratory whose accreditation has been accepted by the CPSC.

claim: All manufacturers of children's products must conduct periodic testing.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: All manufacturers of children's products must conduct periodic testing.

claim: Without a production testing plan or ISO/IEC 17025 lab testing, the periodic testing interval may not exceed one year.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: may not exceed one year

claim: With a production testing plan, samples must be third-party tested at least once every two years.

claim: A material change means any change in the product's design, manufacturing process, or sourcing of component parts that a manufacturer exercising due care knows, or should know, could affect the product's ability to comply with the applicable rules.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: any change in the product's design, manufacturing process, or sourcing of component parts that a manufacturer exercising due care knows, or should know
